goal: Finish the notification story that 022-problem-notifications deliberately left half-built, closing the four gaps named in its own Out of Scope list, in dependency order.

entries.title: Per-event read state and snooze
entries.description:
Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/notifications.md in full — its goal paragraph, the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" bullet list (notification_states, attention events, the DAL readers, the routes, the components, the all-or-none env groups, the worker tick) and the "Rules for every entry" list (leave the repo working and say what it does not do; explicitly reverse shipped decisions and record the replacement in docs/decisions.md next to the original including what happens to data written under the old rule; committed SQL migration with `pnpm db:check` green and safe to apply to a live install with existing rows; project isolation enforced by the test harness; role-aware per N10; prefer existing UI primitives and the docket-ui skill plus docs/design-system.md; secrets never leak; any browser/screenshot/visual-judgement task goes last in tasks.md). Also read specs/022-problem-notifications/ (spec, data model, contracts, review) and decisions N1-N12 in docs/decisions.md in full, because this entry deliberately reverses shipped decisions and the spec must name which ones and why.

Scope of this entry: let a person dismiss one problem, or snooze it until later, without touching the rest. This reverses decision N3 (one forward-only watermark per project, never one row per event) and N2's rule that a problem stays unread until you mark the whole project read; say so explicitly and record the replacement decisions in docs/decisions.md next to the originals, including what happens to data already written under the old rule. Keep `seen_seq` as a floor — everything at or below it is read, and "Mark all as read" still just bumps the floor — and add a sparse per-event table above the floor for individually read and snoozed events, so row growth stays bounded and the floor can absorb and prune the sparse rows. That bound is the point of the entry: N3 avoided per-event rows for cost reasons and this must not reintroduce them unbounded. A snoozed problem leaves the count and the panel until its time passes, then returns unread; snoozing is personal and never hides the event from Activity (N5's spirit). Define what a snooze means for an event whose target has since been retried or resolved, and what happens when the floor rises past a snoozed event. Update the count query, `createNotificationsRepo` and `createNotificationsSetReader` in src/server/dal/notifications.ts, both /api/me/notifications routes, the panel rows (per-row "Mark read" and "Snooze", keyboard reachable, announced through the LiveRegion) and ProblemsCallout.

Testing the author attached to this entry: counting with a mix of floor-read, individually-read, snoozed and expired-snooze events; pruning when the floor rises; concurrent mark-read from two tabs; snooze expiry at a DST boundary; membership removal still deleting everything; project isolation.

Must NOT take on: per-kind or per-platform preferences (owned by entry 2, notification-preferences); any email (owned by entry 3, email-delivery); replacing the 60-second poll (owned by entry 4, realtime-updates); notifications for successes or retries, which are not in this roadmap at all — N1 stands.
entries.rationale: The author's reason is the cost bound: N3 avoided per-event rows deliberately, so the floor-plus-sparse-rows design is what makes per-event dismissal affordable, and keeping row growth bounded "is the point of the entry". It is first because the read/snooze state and the count-route payload shape that later entries consume are defined here.

entries.title: Per-kind and per-platform preferences
entries.description:
Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/notifications.md in full — its goal paragraph, the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" bullet list (notification_states keyed (project_id, user_id) with `muted`; attention events per N1 in src/lib/activity/outcomes.ts; the DAL readers; the /notifications page and actions.ts; the notifications components) and the "Rules for every entry" list (leave the repo working and say what it does not do; explicitly reverse shipped decisions and record the replacement in docs/decisions.md next to the original including the fate of existing data; committed SQL migration with `pnpm db:check` green and safe to apply to a live install with existing rows, never requiring an operator to reset notification state; project isolation; role-aware per N10 with nothing owner-only but server configuration; existing UI primitives, the docket-ui skill and docs/design-system.md, full keyboard use and labelled controls; secrets never leak; browser or visual-judgement tasks last in tasks.md). Also read specs/022-problem-notifications/ and decisions N1-N12 in docs/decisions.md in full — N1, N6 and N10 constrain this entry directly.

Scope of this entry: replace the single per-project `muted` boolean with preferences a person can set per attention kind (the four from N1) and per platform, with the project level becoming a roll-up — "all off" is the old mute, and the UI must still offer that in one click. Migrate every existing `muted = true` row to all-kinds-off so no one's choice is lost, and say in docs/decisions.md what `muted` becomes (kept as a derived column, or dropped). Preferences gate the bell count, the panel, the callout and — once email-delivery lands — what is eligible to be mailed, so the shape settled here is the shape email consumes. Keep N6's fresh-start rule: turning a kind back on marks that kind read at that moment rather than delivering a backlog. Extend /notifications (src/app/notifications/page.tsx) from a list of on/off toggles into a per-project grid, keep the same control on each project's settings page for every member role, and keep both usable with no client JavaScript.

Testing the author attached to this entry: migration of muted rows; counting under each preference combination; per-platform filtering against accounts that were later removed; the fresh-start rule; defaults for a new member and a new project; and authz — a person may only edit their own preferences.

Must NOT take on: quiet hours — the author's stated reason is that quiet hours are a delivery-timing rule with no meaning for an in-app badge, and entry 3 (email-delivery) owns them; any email (entry 3, email-delivery); changing which outcomes are attention events, since N1 stands; real-time transport (entry 4, realtime-updates).
entries.rationale: The author gives two reasons: no one's existing choice may be lost (hence the migration of every `muted = true` row to all-kinds-off), and this entry must precede email because "the shape settled here is the shape email consumes" — preferences gate what is eligible to be mailed. Quiet hours are excluded on the stated ground that they are a delivery-timing rule with no meaning for an in-app badge.

entries.title: Email delivery
entries.description:
Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/notifications.md in full — its goal paragraph, the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" bullet list (invitation delivery already behind the InvitationDelivery / defaultInvitationDelivery interface in src/server/services/invitations/delivery.ts:16-21 injected at index.ts:67, with Docket having no mailer of any kind today; the all-or-none env group pattern of STORAGE_GROUP in src/server/env.ts:72-88; the worker tick at /api/internal/tick with WORKER_INTERVAL_SECONDS, RUN_WORKER_IN_PROCESS and budgets in src/server/scheduler/config.ts as the only recurring server-side execution Docket has) and the "Rules for every entry" list — in particular the secrets rule: SMTP credentials, signed unsubscribe tokens and recipient addresses are never logged, never in error messages, never in attempt summaries, and the secret-scan test must stay green. Also read specs/022-problem-notifications/ and decisions N1-N12 in docs/decisions.md in full, and record any reversal next to the original decision.

Scope of this entry: give Docket its first mailer and use it to deliver problems to people who are not signed in. A `Mailer` interface mirroring InvitationDelivery in shape, a default SMTP implementation, and an all-or-none SMTP env group following STORAGE_GROUP (src/server/env.ts:72-88) — email off when the group is unset, exactly as media is off without S3, and a startup validation issue if a satellite variable is set without the group. Per-user choice of immediate or a daily digest at a chosen local hour, honouring the preferences from notification-preferences (entry 2) and the read/snooze state from per-event-read-state (entry 1): never mail a problem the person has already read, dismissed or snoozed, and assemble the digest at send time rather than queueing per event. Quiet hours belong here — within them, immediate mail defers to the next allowed hour rather than being dropped. Digests run on the existing worker tick, inside its budget, with per-user send bookkeeping that survives a crash and never double-sends. Every email carries a one-click unsubscribe that works without a login (a signed, scoped, expiring token — never a bare user id) and lands on a page explaining exactly what was turned off. A delivery log in the shape of the webhook delivery log (src/server/services/webhooks/deliver.ts, src/server/dal/webhooks.ts) records attempts, failures and bounces without storing message bodies. Retrofit defaultInvitationDelivery so invitations are emailed when SMTP is configured and fall back to today's copy-the-link flow when it is not, and update docs/build-prompt.md:85, docs/accounts.md:44 and .env.example accordingly.

Testing the author attached to this entry: the env group (all-or-none, satellite-without-group, off-when-unset); immediate vs digest selection; quiet-hours deferral across DST and across time zones; no double-send under a crashed and retried tick; read, snoozed and preference-filtered events excluded; unsubscribe token signing and expiry plus tamper rejection; bounce handling; invitation fallback both ways; and that no SMTP credential or recipient address reaches a log line.

Must NOT take on: push or chat delivery — webhooks still cover automation, see docs/n8n.md; notifications for successes; per-event actions inside the email beyond unsubscribe; real-time transport (entry 4, realtime-updates).
entries.rationale: The author's reasons: Docket has no mailer today and invitation delivery was put behind an interface precisely so one could be dropped in (docs/build-prompt.md:85), so this entry both adds the mailer and redeems that promise; email must come after entries 1 and 2 because it consumes their read/snooze state and preference shape; quiet hours live here rather than in entry 2 because they are a delivery-timing rule; and the digest is assembled at send time, not queued per event, so already-read or snoozed problems are never mailed.

entries.title: Real-time updates
entries.description:
Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/notifications.md in full — its goal paragraph, the "Behaviour on `main` that every entry builds on" bullet list (the /api/me/notifications 60-second count poll per N12, the notifications components including poll.ts and NotificationBellClient.tsx, the DAL readers and the one sanctioned cross-project reader, and the worker tick with RUN_WORKER_IN_PROCESS) and the "Rules for every entry" list (leave the repo working and say what it does not do; explicitly reverse shipped decisions and record the replacement in docs/decisions.md next to the original; project isolation; existing UI primitives, the docket-ui skill and docs/design-system.md with screen-reader announcements only on meaningful change per N12; secrets never leak; any browser, screenshot or visual-judgement task goes last in tasks.md). Also read specs/022-problem-notifications/ and decisions N1-N12 in docs/decisions.md in full — this entry replaces N12's poll, so the spec must name that reversal and record the replacement decision.

Scope of this entry: replace N12's 60-second poll with a server push so a problem appears in the bell within seconds. Server-Sent Events over one authenticated endpoint, carrying the same payload shape the count route returns after per-event-read-state (entry 1) changed it. poll.ts and NotificationBellClient.tsx become a fallback that still works when the stream cannot connect, and the count must still render server-side with no client JavaScript at all. The deployment constraints are the entry's real content, not an afterthought: Docket is a single container behind a reverse proxy that may buffer or time out long-lived responses, may run several web processes, and RUN_WORKER_IN_PROCESS means the writer may not be the process holding the connection — so decide and record how an event reaches every connected process, how many connections one install will hold, what happens when the cap is reached, and how the stream is closed on sign-out, session expiry and membership removal. Document the proxy configuration it needs in docs/deployment.md.

Testing the author attached to this entry: auth and project scoping on the stream; a client that reconnects after a dropped connection without missing or double-counting events; fallback to polling when SSE is unavailable; the connection cap; teardown on sign-out and on membership removal; and no leak of another person's counts.

Must NOT take on: Web Push or service workers — the author calls this a separate problem (OS-level delivery, VAPID keys and a service worker lifecycle) and says it is not in this roadmap; changing what is counted or who is notified; any change to email cadence (owned by entry 3, email-delivery).
entries.rationale: The author's reason for placing this last is that the stream carries "the same payload shape the count route returns after per-event-read-state changed it", so the payload must settle first; and the reason the entry exists at all is latency — a problem should appear in the bell within seconds instead of up to 60. The author also insists the deployment constraints (buffering proxy, multiple web processes, RUN_WORKER_IN_PROCESS) are the entry's real content rather than an afterthought.
